melodicFingerprints: Hook E–G–A–Bb, bars 1–2 and 5–6, then the descent A–G–E–D at bars 3 and 7.
Bars 21–24 hold E against Bb. Bars 25–28 repeat A–G–E–D.
protectedLandmarks: Bar 8 is 3/4. Every other bar is 4/4.
Printed words: Crooked, dry, physical; Bass leads — guitar follows; OPEN DUO; wrong turn — let it stand.
Guitar rest at bar 30. No rehearsal marks. No chord symbols.
blueprint.originalBassIdentity: Bass moves from bar 1 (E–A–G) and does not wait for the guitar. Guitar octave-change is 0, so written guitar pitch is sounding pitch. CBV is no-change.
strongestPassages: No listening rank. Notation only. The leadsheet interruptions that the performance keeps are bar 8 in 3/4, the E/Bb argument at 21–24, and the guitar rest at 30 before Bb–E–A.
A–H were read and not spliced. C suggested a foreign dyad. H suggested a pentatonic field against the bass. G suggested long guitar silence. Those ideas were rewritten.
blueprint.harmonicJourney: Locked bass stays the floor: E/A/G/Bb, then F/Ab around bars 8–12, F under the E/Bb hold, F at the end. Guitar adds three turns: Bb/D in bar 4, C/Eb against bass A in bar 9 (the Ab triad arrives late and misses), Db/F/Ab in bar 18 moving by one common-tone step to D/F/Ab in bar 28. No ii–V–I.
blueprint.contrapuntalOpportunities: Bass leads. Guitar withholds through the F of bar 8, through most of bars 9–12, and through the bass scale in bar 16, then answers late. No second line runs under the whole tune.
blueprint.dramaticClimax: Not auditioned. The densest guitar moment is the Db triad in bar 18. The close does not peak. Bar 32 lets E/Bb stand on low F.
blueprint.thematicReturn: Bars 3 and 7 state A–G–E–D. Bar 25 states it again. Bar 26 turns the last note to Bb. Bar 28 keeps the rhythm and changes the last chord. Bar 29 states the hook and withholds its closing E. Bar 32 gives that E back, with Bb.
blueprint.expectedPerformanceDuration: Quarter = 120, and sound tempo 120. 31 bars of 4/4 plus bar 8 in 3/4 = 1:03.50.

motif.name: hook
motif.note: Opening guitar hook. The 3/4 bar and the E/Bb hold are separate events, not extra statements of this hook.

landmarks.role: hook and the A–G–E–D answer, twice

narrative.name: Hook
narrative.job: Printed instruction: crooked, dry, physical. Hook twice, with the descending answer.

narrative.name: Short bar
narrative.job: Bar 8 cuts the hook. Bass F is heard alone. Bars 9–11 answer late. Bar 12 names Ab on the last beat, against bass A.

narrative.name: Hook again
narrative.job: Two rough hooks exit to F, then to Bb. Bar 16 leaves the bass scale alone until a late Bb. Bar 17 ends on Ab. Bar 18 is the Db triad.

narrative.name: Hold
narrative.job: E then Bb, then E alone, then Bb before E, then the E/Bb dyad falling to D.

narrative.name: Descent and stop
narrative.job: Descent, a Bb ending, a late E–D, then D/F/Ab. Hook stops early in bar 29. Guitar rest at 30. Bb–E–A, then E/Bb. Let the wrong turn stand.

seams.job: Rest, then the last two bars

mci.continuity: The E–G–A–Bb hook and the A–G–E–D descent stay recognisable. Bar 8 stays in 3/4. The bass event stream stays.
mci.innovation: Familiar phrases change direction: early D in bar 6, cut hook in bar 8, F inside the rough hook, Ab instead of the closing E in bar 17, reversed E/Bb in bar 23. The short bar stays in 3/4. No section letters.

cbv.note: No bass proposal. Principal bass stays the leadsheet stream.

radicalProfile.note: WWH starting profile. Listening guide, not a note count.

gce.weakest: Cadential clarity of bars 9–12. V1.0 left that F-world phrase without a guitar arrival. V1.1 bar 12 beat 4 is Ab4 against bass A.
